newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African gives himself up for killing two Britons.
newsitem.headline: S.African gives himself up for killing two Britons.

text.p: A 26-year-old man surrendered to police saying he was responsibile for the murder of two British tourists in South Africa's Zulu heartland four years ago, a police spokesman said on Monday.

Julie Godwin, from Northampton, England, was on holiday with her friend Elizabeth Over, who was living in South Africa, when they were killed on a deserted stretch of beach on November 30, 1992, police spokesman Bala Naidoo said in a statement.

The two women had been hacked to death and their bodies mutilated during the attack, north of Sodwana Bay. Their four-wheel drive truck was stuck in the sand and splattered with blood. Tools and money had been stolen.
Godwin was survived by her husband, Tim -- who was due to come out to join her on holiday with their daughter Sophie, then almost two years old.
The suspected killer, whose name is being withheld, gave himself up to police at the weekend.
"The detectives are at present investigating and evaluating the claims made by the man," Naidoo said.
"It's quite possible that the murders haunted him," Naidoo told Reuters, adding that other suspects were being sought for questioning.
